Recommended architecture (based only on the provided OFBiz docs)

High‑level approach
- Build on the Global Chart of Accounts template: add any new accounts you need there first, then assign them into your Company chart (Chart of Accounts) so they are active for the organisation [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0].

Which accounts to create / assign
- Create a small, consistent set of accounts per store so you can report profitability and reconcile cash per store. for example (per store):
  - Store Revenue (sales) account
  - Store Cash/Bank (till/banking) account
  - Store Inventory on-hand account
  - Store COGS account
  - Store Inter-store Transfer / Inventory Movement account(s)
- Create central/company-level accounts for procurement/central warehouse (e.g., Central Inventory, Central AP) and assign those too. Add these accounts in the Global template, then create assignments into the Company chart [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_AssignGlAccount.adoc-0].

Mapping transaction types to accounts
- Use the Organization GL Settings / GL Account Type Defaults to map transaction types (Accounts Payable, Accounts Receivable, Inventory, etc.) to the GL Account Ids you created. The mapping uses the GL Account Id to determine which account a transaction posts to (so set these to the per-store or central accounts as required by the transaction source) [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_GlAccountNavigate.adoc-0].

Product-level detail and COGS
- Use Product GL Account entries to get product-level posting defaults (e.g., track COGS or AR by product). Product GL Account maps Product + Account Type to a GL account and is used to specify the default account for product transactions (one side of the journal) for more detailed tracking [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_EditProductGlAccounts.adoc-0].

Internal transfers between warehouses/stores
- Treat inter-store/internal transfers as postings between the store inventory accounts and the central inventory account (or between store inventory accounts). Ensure you have dedicated transfer accounts or use the inter-store transfer account(s) you created and map the transaction type in GL Account Type Defaults so transfers generate the correct debit/credit [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_GlAccountNavigate.adoc-0].

Operational notes / cautions
- You do not need to use every account in the Global template; pick/assign only those you will use, or add new accounts into the Global template and then assign them into the Company chart [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-1].
- If you create/replace accounts, remember to check and update all GL defaults (GL Account Type Defaults, Product GL defaults, etc.) so transactions continue to post to the intended accounts [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_ListGlAccountOrganization.adoc-0] [doc:applications/accounting/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/HELP_GlAccountNavigate.adoc-0].

Short answer: This looks like configuration/demo-data misuse, not an OFBiz code bug. You loaded the demo data (which includes an "admin" party and default passwords) and either left admin/default accounts enabled or gave democustomer permissions that allow editing via the Party Manager UI. See points and fixes below.

What’s happening (why your steps allow it)
- The demo data includes an "admin" party and default userlogins (default password "ofbiz") — so the account exists and is editable if someone has access to the Party Manager/edit UI [7045138-8].  
- The Party Manager UI lets you view a party’s usernames and use the "Edit" action to change a user login’s password (that is normal behavior of the Party Manager) [170266058-36].  
- OFBiz security is driven by permissions, roles and groups; if democustomer has permissions (or role-limited permissions) that permit access to the Party Manager or user-login edit actions, they will be able to see/edit parties that those permissions allow [48202125-0].

What you did wrong
- You loaded demo data and left demo accounts in their default state (and/or granted democustomer permissions that permit editing). The documentation explicitly warns not to use demo credentials and to change/disable demo userlogins after loading demo data [7045142-1][7045138-8].

Immediate fixes to secure the instance
1. Change or disable all demo userlogins (admin, flexadmin, demoadmin, etc.) immediately via Party Manager while logged in as a trusted admin; edit user names to change passwords or disable accounts [7045142-1][170266058-36].  
2. Review and remove any security groups/roles/permissions from democustomer that grant Party Manager or user-edit rights (use Party Manager to inspect assigned groups/roles/permissions) [48202125-0][170266058-36].  
3. Do not use demo credentials on any exposed server — follow the deployment security best practices in the guide (change passwords, disable unwanted logins, shut down unused webapps) [7045142-1][7045138-8].

If you want, tell me the exact security groups/roles assigned to democustomer (shown in Party Manager) and I’ll point which permissions to remove based on the security model [48202125-0].

Short diagnosis
- The JVM is spending almost all time in GC (GC overhead limit exceeded). In OFBiz this often happens when the Entity Engine caches (which use SoftReferences) are repeatedly cleared during GC or when the heap is too small for large result sets [48201990-29][7045138-31].

Recommended actions (concise)
1) Increase JVM heap and set a higher initial heap:
   - Use larger -Xms and -Xmx (examples in the docs; e.g. a typical production suggestion is -Xms256M -Xmx2048M and aim for ~75% of machine RAM for max heap). Make the small size (Xms) fairly high (even equal to Xmx) to avoid repeated GC/soft-ref clearing [7045138-31].

2) Use WebTools cache/GC controls and cache configuration:
   - From WebTools use the Cache & Debug / Cache Management pages to view/clear caches and force garbage collection as a temporary mitigation. For permanent cache tuning adjust cache.properties as documented [doc:framework/webtools/src/docs/asciidoc/_include/webtools-main.adoc-0][48201990-29].

3) Avoid pulling enormous result sets in the UI:
   - Don’t navigate WebTools to retrieve tens of millions of rows in one operation; prefer limiting/pagination at the query level or more selective filters. For database-intensive operations focus on how the DB handles the queries rather than relying on in-memory caching [7045138-31][48201990-31].

4) Consider architectural scaling if this is expected workload:
   - For very large datasets consider scaling beyond a single instance (load balancing / multiple nodes) and optimize DB queries rather than relying on a single JVM to hold huge lists [7045138-31].

If you want, tell me your current -Xms/-Xmx values and whether you are using default cache.properties and I’ll point to which setting to change next.

High-level process to manage a purchase-order (PO) invoice in Apache OFBiz

1) Prepare master data (suppliers, products, GL/accounts)
   - Set up the supplier (vendor) and product/party/payment info before purchasing [7766058-0][165223099-14].

2) Create and approve the Purchase Order
   - Create a PO for the supplier and the items you need; approve it per your procurement workflow [doc:docs/asciidoc/user-manual.adoc-0][165223099-14].

3) Receive goods/services (shipment/receipt)
   - Record goods receipts or service delivery against the PO so quantities and dates are available for matching [doc:docs/asciidoc/user-manual.adoc-0].

4) Create / enter the Purchase Invoice
   - Enter the supplier invoice in Accounts Payable and link it to the PO (and the receipt) so the system can match invoiced quantities/prices to what was ordered/received [doc:docs/asciidoc/user-manual.adoc-0].

5) Match and approve the invoice (2‑ or 3‑way matching)
   - Perform PO-to-invoice (and receipt) matching; resolve discrepancies (quantity, price, freight, taxes) and approve the invoice for payment [doc:docs/asciidoc/user-manual.adoc-0].

6) Pay the invoice and post accounting
   - Execute payment runs and post the accounting entries once the invoice is approved; configuration for payments/GL is covered in the business setup docs [165223099-14][doc:docs/asciidoc/user-manual.adoc-0].

Short recommended approach (based only on the provided OFBiz docs):

1) Choose your tenancy model
   - OFBiz multi-tenancy is implemented as one database per tenant by default; a default DB still exists [14814279-1].  
   - For multi-merchant scenarios where merchants share physical facilities, consider using ProductStore as the merchant-account/isolation field instead of per-merchant DBs (avoid fragmentation) [430408956-2].

2) Tenant selection / authentication flow
   - Users log into a specific tenant by supplying a tenant ID on the login form or by using a tenant-specific URL/domain. The tenant identifier is how OFBiz selects the tenant DB/context for the session [14814279-1].  
   - Frontend support for tenant-specific domains and tenant login is explicitly supported (tenant-specific domain names, multi-site per tenant) — you can run a front store on a tenant-specific domain like "abc.com" [49579254-1][49579254-2].

3) Frontend (React) architecture
   - Build the React app as an API-driven frontend that consumes OFBiz services/APIs rather than embedding OFBiz UI. The community guidance is to expose backend capabilities via APIs so modern frontends (React) can be used [27841316-34].  
   - Ensure the React frontend includes/forwards the tenant identifier (tenant ID or domain-derived tenant) on authentication and subsequent API calls so OFBiz can route to the correct tenant DB/context [14814279-1][49579254-2].

4) Configuration and tenancy-specific data
   - Make configuration attributes tenant-specific where needed (OFBiz multitenancy extensions support tenant-specific configuration) [49579254-1].  
   - When using shared logical merchants (ProductStore) keep per-merchant isolation on indexed fields (productStoreId) rather than separate DBs when the business requires shared facilities/data [430408956-2].

5) Scalability / operational note
   - Multitenancy is designed so tenants don’t require server restarts to add/manage tenant data; aim for DB-driven, self-service tenant operations rather than manual server-side installs [14814279-1].  
   - Prefer the API-driven integration pattern so you can scale and evolve the React frontend independently of OFBiz internals [27841316-34].

References used: [14814279-1], [49579254-1], [49579254-2], [430408956-2], [27841316-34].

There is no built‑in, documented ECA for SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED in the excerpts you provided. The docs only show the sales-return ECA pattern and general ECA/SECA usage; they do not describe a supplier/purchase-return ECA for SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED [73634379-15] [73634379-17] [7045171-16].

You can implement the behavior yourself by adding a service-eca for the purchase‑return update service that mirrors the sales one: trigger on commit, require statusId = SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED and oldStatusId != SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED, and call the debit‑note (purchase return invoice) creation service. Use <set> entries if you need to map/insert parameters for the called service. The Service ECA syntax and examples are shown in the docs (use event="commit", <condition> and <action> entries) [7045171-16]. SECA/service-eca files are validated against service-eca.xsd and can be enabled/loaded as described in the SECA tutorial [93325429-48].

Example skeleton (pattern from the docs — adapt service names/parameters to your purchase-return services):

    <service-eca>
      <eca service="yourPurchaseReturnUpdateService" event="commit">
        <condition field-name="statusId" operator="equals" value="SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED"/>
        <condition field-name="oldStatusId" operator="not-equals" value="SUP_RETURN_COMPLETED"/>
        <!-- optional <set> mappings here to supply required params to the invoice/debit-note service -->
        <action service="yourCreatePurchaseReturnInvoiceService" mode="sync"/>
      </eca>
    </service-eca>

References: ECA usage and <set> tip [7045171-16]; SECA/service-eca enablement and example [93325429-48]; sales-return process (context for the sales ECA pattern) [73634379-15] [73634379-17].

Most likely cause: the Context Security Filter (the entry point for all web requests) is configured to allow the whole /images path, so the first web request/initialization will touch that images directory. If that directory is a mounted filesystem with many files it can delay startup/first-request handling [50233547-2].

What to try
- Restrict the allowedPaths in /WEB-INF/web.xml so you do not allow the entire /images tree (use specific files or subdirectories instead, e.g. '/images/some-subdir' or '/images/some-subdir/*' rather than '/images') — the CSF supports directory, file and wildcard patterns as shown in the docs [50233547-2].
- If you must serve a very large/mounted image tree, keep it unmounted until OFBiz has started (you observed this speeds startup), or move frequently accessed images to a smaller served subtree.
- Ensure the server has adequate resources for your dataset (disk and RAM recommendations in the requirements) if you continue to serve many assets from the app host [13271447-2].

References: Context Security Filter and allowedPaths usage [50233547-2]; system sizing note [13271447-2].

Key confirmations and caveats from the docs:
- Use non-sales types so billing ECAs never fire (no invoice/payment/GL). Auto-invoice/payment are gated on SALES types, so a FULFILLMENT_ORDER / FULFIL_SHIPMENT prevents order-to-cash by construction [430409055-3].  
- Make FULFILLMENT_ORDER standalone (do NOT make it a child of SALES_ORDER) or sales logic can re-attach via parent-type checks [430409055-2].  
- Tenancy-by-data is the documented approach: one ProductStore per merchant (payToPartyId = merchant), ProductStoreFacility to map warehouse, ProductStoreRole for API grants, and InventoryItem.ownerPartyId to tell apart commingled stock — no new tables needed [430409055-5].  
- Important operational gaps: the standard warehouse pipeline and one-call shipping services are sales-coupled and won’t work for non-sales orders. You must drive lower-level services in sequence (receive, storeOrder/approve, reserve, pick, createShipmentRouteSegment, createShipment → issue items → updateShipment statuses, poll for tracking). There’s no complete non-sales "issue to shipment" service — hand-roll issuance with createItemIssuance + createInventoryItemDetail and be careful not to subtract ATP twice (set availableToPromiseDiff = 0) [430409055-4].  
- Summary: your design (non-sales types + stock-based tenancy) is exactly what the doc recommends; expect to implement lower-level shipping/issuance logic rather than reuse sales shortcuts [430409055-0][430409055-3][430409055-4][430409055-5][430409055-2].

- Bank statements: use states such as CREATED, IN PROCESS and RECONCILED.

Short answer: pagination is driven by the performFind call and the list-name/result-map-list mapping. Make sure the list name, paginate-target and the performFind field-maps for viewIndex/viewSize match what the grid/form uses. See steps below.

What to check/fix
- paginate-target: the list form must have paginate-target set to the screen that displays the form — this is required to enable pagination for multi-page lists [170266058-26].
- list-name vs result-map-list: the list-name you give the grid/form must exactly match the service result-map-list where the performFind returns the rows. In the tutorial the form has list-name="listIt" and the performFind uses result-map-list="listIt" — if you rename the list you must update the result-map-list too [170266058-25].
- pass page and size parameters: the performFind/service must receive viewIndex and viewSize (mapped from parameters.viewIndex and parameters.viewSize) so the service returns the correct page. The tutorial shows field-maps for viewIndex and viewSize in the performFind call [170266058-25]. If those mappings are missing the service will keep returning the first page.
- items-per-page behavior: the grid will show whatever the service returns for the requested viewSize; if viewSize is larger than the total rows you naturally get all rows. Control the per-page value by supplying parameters.viewSize (and viewIndex) to performFind [170266058-25].
- other notes: performFind is the service that implements the paging logic (see services/FindServices) so ensure you are invoking it properly and mapping inputs/outputs [170266058-26]. There are known UI-related pagination issues (e.g. widget.form.defaultViewSize / last-page button) reported in the project notes if you still see odd behavior [7766043-10].

Minimal checklist to fix your plugin
1. In the grid/form: set type="list", list-name="yourListName" and paginate-target="theScreenName" [170266058-26][170266058-25].  
2. In actions/service call: call performFind (or performFindList) and include field-map entries:
   - result-map-list="yourListName" (must match list-name)  
   - field-map viewIndex from-field="parameters.viewIndex"  
   - field-map viewSize from-field="parameters.viewSize"  
   (follow the tutorial example) [170266058-25].  
3. Verify the incoming request supplies parameters.viewIndex and parameters.viewSize (or let the UI supply them). If you still see wrong counts, check for known pagination bugs in the project notes [7766043-10].

References: tutorial examples and explanations of list-name, paginate-target, viewIndex/viewSize and performFind usage [170266058-26][170266058-25]; note about known pagination/UI issues [7766043-10].

Short answers:

1) Yes — async services are run by the job scheduler which uses a thread pool (one poller thread + invoker threads). The number of concurrent threads is bounded by the pool configuration (max-threads); invoker threads are reused and each can process multiple jobs (the jobs attribute) before being destroyed. So running a service 1000 times will not necessarily create 1000 threads — at most max-threads invoker threads (plus the poller) will be created and they will handle the jobs over time [48201960-3].

2) Yes — you can change the pool behavior via the thread-pool configuration. Relevant attributes include min-threads and max-threads (to set the pool size), and other controls such as jobs (max jobs per invoker), ttl, wait-millis, poll-enabled and poll-db-millis [48201960-3]. The async mode for service invocation is selected with mode="async" (e.g. via the ofbiz:service tag) which causes the scheduler to be used [50233686-9][48201960-3].

Short answers and how to fix

1) Pagination not advancing
- Pagination requires the list form to have paginate-target set to the screen that hosts the list and the server-side find service to receive the paging parameters (viewIndex, viewSize). If those aren’t passed the service will return the whole set (or the same page) and pagination appears to repeat or show all rows [170266058-26][170266058-25].
- Make sure your actions/service call maps viewIndex and viewSize from the request parameters into the performFind/performFindList service (example uses field-map entries from parameters.viewIndex and parameters.viewSize). That tells the service which page/size to return [170266058-25].
- If you still see navigation buttons misbehaving, be aware there are known issues in some builds (e.g. the “last” button can be unreliable in some cases) — you may need to check for that bug in your OFBiz version [7766043-10].

2) Renaming the list breaks results
- The list-name in the form must match the service’s result-map-list. The tutorial uses list-name="listIt" and the performFind service returns its results in result-map-list="listIt". If you rename the list you must change result-map-list (and any other references) accordingly; otherwise the grid won’t receive the returned rows [170266058-25][170266058-26].

Concrete checklist to fix your grid
- Set paginate-target on the list form to the correct screen (as in the tutorial) [170266058-26].  
- Use the standard performFind/performFindList service (or mirror its input mappings). In the form’s <service> element map:
  - inputFields/entityName/orderBy as needed and
  - viewIndex <- parameters.viewIndex
  - viewSize  <- parameters.viewSize
  so the service pages correctly [170266058-25].  
- Make sure list-name and service result-map-list match (or update both) so the returned list is bound to the grid [170266058-25].  
- If after that pagination still misbehaves, check your OFBiz version for known pagination bugs (see note about inconsistent “last” button) [7766043-10].

What to do

  <TenantComponent tenantId="YOUR_TENANT_ID" componentName="yourComponentName"/> [14814279-9].
- Install/load the component data for that tenant. Use the multitenant install/load commands or run the installer with the tenant's delegator, for example:
  java -Xmx512m -XX:MaxPermSize=128m -jar ofbiz.jar -install -readers=seed -delegator=default#DEMO1
